source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Power on and boot in BIOS.
2. Change all/random setting to non-default in this BIOS function.
3. Save and reboot.
4. Boot in to BIOS and  check your setting still exist.
5. Press load default,save and reboot.
6. Boot in to BIOS,setting in this function should match the SPEC.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. No error log happen.
2. Normal reboot ,no hang、crash happen.
3. Check your setting still exist.
4. The default setting should matches SPEC."

original_test_intent: The item names an actual firmware image update, whereas the supplied procedure tests arbitrary setting persistence and Load Default. The source does not define which component is updated, the source/target version, the flash trigger, activation sequence or recovery acceptance.
original_method: Use the BIOS Firmware Update page but apply a generic non-default/save/reboot/persistence/default workflow. No validated image, update command/path, version direction, power requirement or rollback procedure is specified.
manual_activity: After the source is corrected, a qualified engineer must authorize and operate the BIOS update path, monitor any non-interruptible phase and own recovery. Agent package verification and post-update identity checks cannot supply the missing update procedure.
required_inputs: Corrected case-specific update sequence and PASS criteria
Target component plus current, source and target firmware identities
Vendor-approved signed image/package with hash and compatibility
Update, activation, configuration-preservation and rollback policy
Independent BMC/OOB or hardware recovery, stable power and maintenance window
Expected final firmware and configuration state
safety_requirements: Do not interpret all/random or generic setting changes as authorization to flash.
Do not stage or write firmware until exact compatibility, integrity, version direction and recovery are approved.
Ensure the recovery path remains independent of the component being updated.
Never interrupt a confirmed non-interruptible flash; stop before commit if power, console or recovery is degraded.
Do not automatically rollback or retry after failure.
Preserve all first-failure and updater evidence.
agent_execution_scope: Validate an approved package's public metadata, hash/signature, compatibility mapping and version direction before any write.
Collect read-only pre/post firmware, boot, log and BMC identity after engineer-authorized execution.
Do not invent an updater command, initiate a flash, decide rollback or issue PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Replace the generic setting workflow with a vendor-supported update lifecycle and aligned criteria.
Approve the exact image, direction, activation, preservation and recovery plan and perform the firmware operation.
Evaluate final identity, configuration and recovery evidence and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its refusal of agent BIOS interaction is safe, but there is no actual update command or valid method to assess; the described generic save/default operation is not equivalent to firmware update.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No update command may be recommended without platform/vendor identity and official package documentation. Preserve the BIOS path named by the item and reject generic software flashing as a substitute.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The source null script and 5/20-minute fields are recorded, but the generic timing cannot be assumed sufficient for a firmware write and no execution is authorized.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Define baseline firmware/configuration, verify a vendor-signed compatible image, perform the approved BIOS update under stable power and independent recovery, verify activation/version/configuration/boot/management health, and use rollback only under an approved failure decision.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Undetermined until the target component, board and firmware package are identified.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record current/target firmware, BIOS UI/updater, BMC, recovery image and any verification-tool versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Exact vendor update, compatibility, configuration-preservation and recovery documentation is mandatory.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces an inapplicable generic default-setting template with a controlled firmware version transition.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Restores the named update coverage; it must also explicitly define whether configuration defaults/preservation are separate acceptance dimensions.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Corrected procedure, exact package, version transition, activation and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: No generic public command is safe for an unidentified platform or component.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve a particular upgrade, downgrade or same-version reflash, but must state that direction and image. Completing one approved transition cannot be generalized to other images or mechanisms.
expected_evidence: Corrected procedure/criteria and owner-approved update plan
Platform/target identity, source/target versions, image signature/hash and compatibility
Pre-update configuration, recovery and stable-power checks
Complete BIOS update/activation console evidence without hidden retry
Post-update identity, configuration, boot/BMC health, recovery disposition and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The item requires an image update, but Procedure and Criteria only exercise generic setting persistence and Load Default. Those operations cannot establish that firmware was validated, written, activated or recovered.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The destructive core operation lacks an applicable procedure, target and acceptance semantics. This exceeds missing project parameters; executing the available generic steps would not test the named intent and guessing a flash path would be unsafe.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keeps the conservative human boundary but rejects its generic-setting interpretation.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Adopts its vendor image, integrity, stable-power and recovery gates and aligns the top-level status with its explicit execution block.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Records a genuine item/procedure conflict and requires case-specific correction rather than silently treating an update as a BIOS field.

review_improvement: Prevents a destructive firmware update from being reviewed or executed using an unrelated persistence/default template and demands complete version-transition evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: A firmware update is a versioned write and activation lifecycle, not an arbitrary setting. Because no safe update method or acceptance exists in the source, neither manual operation nor agent support can resolve the core semantics; BLOCKED is the only defensible classification.
no_automatic_retry: No firmware update, activation, rollback or recovery action may be retried automatically; preserve the first result and require engineer/vendor disposition.
